high_level_description: Strictly non-photographic, wordless Rio samba-school illustration spanning barracão and parade avenue: one completed allegorical float passes through a narrow starting portal with every module locked in place, while loose replacement sculptures remain inside the workshop, showing that a compiled run keeps its fixed plan and later edits require another version.

compositional_deconstruction.background: The upper third is an open Rio samba-school barracão with high steel rafters, a concrete floor and a wide doorway narrowing into one start portal. The lower two-thirds become a long dark parade avenue bordered by simple cream stands beneath a cobalt night sky. Saturated magenta, turquoise, gold, green and black painted shapes replace photographic depth; no text, number, arrow, banner, logo, screen, book, tablet, diagram panel or national flag appears.

elements.desc: The primary background element, a narrow oxblood-and-gold starting portal fixed between the barracão and parade avenue, with a rigid rectangular opening sized around the completed float. Its closed side rails prevent loose modules from crossing beside the moving structure. The portal has no written school name, countdown number, traffic arrow, judge, royal crest, ticket sign, screen or ceremonial throne.

Single completed samba-school allegorical float moving down the avenue, built from painted wood, hammered foil, papier-mâché and fabric fringe as one coherent vehicle. A turquoise river creature, three gold sun disks and two magenta wing structures are visibly bolted to its frame before the portal. No module is loose, duplicated, transparent, newly appearing, labeled, numbered or connected by arrows.

Five adult barracão artisans working together inside the upper-left workshop, diverse brown skin tones and black hair, plain magenta, green, cobalt and ochre work clothes with protective aprons. Two secure the final hinge while three hold tools beside the portal; none reaches through after the float crosses, and no director occupies a throne, podium, oversized position or exclusive control platform.

Loose replacement modules remaining inside the upper-right barracão: one violet fish head, one green spiral fin and one gold crescent arch arranged on separate wheeled dollies. Each is visibly wider than the portal's side gap and stays behind after the current float enters the avenue. They bear no writing, numeral, arrow, version badge, sacred emblem, human rider or hidden attachment.

Compact group of eight samba-school performers advancing behind the float at lower left, diverse brown skin tones, black hair, coordinated turquoise, magenta and gold costumes with featherless geometric shoulder pieces. Their steps follow the vehicle already on the avenue and no performer carries a loose module, instruction board, flag, written sign, arrow, crown, weapon or modern electronic device.
